name: sigil
description: The Sigil policy language: syntax highlighting, diagnostics, completion, hover, go to definition and formatting through sigil lsp
author: Cedric Specht <cedric@specht-labs.de>

untrustedWorkspaces.description: In an untrusted workspace, the workspace's sigil.path setting is ignored, so a folder you open can't choose which program runs.

virtualWorkspaces.description: Highlighting and snippets work everywhere; the language server needs files on disk.

sigil.path.markdownDescription: The `sigil` binary to run the language server with: an absolute path, a path starting with `~/`, a path relative to the first workspace folder, or a command name looked up on `PATH`. Leave it empty to use the binary bundled with the extension, or `sigil` on `PATH` when there's none.

sigil.server.enabled.markdownDescription: Run `sigil lsp` for diagnostics, completion, hover, go to definition and formatting. Highlighting and snippets work without it.

enumDescriptions: Log each message's method and timing
Log each message with its parameters and result
sigil.trace.server.markdownDescription: How much of each message between VS Code and `sigil lsp` the **Sigil Language Server Trace** output channel logs. The channel only logs messages while its log level is **Trace**: open it in the Output panel and pick Trace from the gear menu.

sigil.checkForUpdates.markdownDescription: Once a day, ask GitHub for the latest Sigil release, and offer to download it when it's newer than this extension. Only VS Code asks: the extension isn't in the Visual Studio Marketplace, so VS Code never updates it. VSCodium, Cursor and the other editors that install it from Open VSX update it themselves.

scripts.build: bun build src/extension.ts --outdir dist --target node --format cjs --external vscode --minify --sourcemap=external
scripts.build:integration: bun build test/integration/suite.ts test/integration/fake-server.ts --outdir dist/test --target node --format cjs --external vscode
